title: A dual-function Cu-MOF–polyaniline nanorod composite for efficient water splitting and enhanced capacitive energy storage
content: In the present study, we synthesized a composite material comprising a copper-based metal–organic framework (Cu-MOF) (BDC) integrated with polyaniline (Pani) nanorods for dual applications in water splitting and capacitive energy storage. The material was characterized using a range of techniques, including X-ray diffraction (XRD), Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), ultraviolet-visible (UV-vis) spectroscopy, thermal analysis, scanning electron microscopy-energy dispersive X-ray analysis (SEM-EDAX), and surface mapping. The electrochemical performance for water splitting was evaluated for both the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and oxygen evolution reaction (OER). The Cu–Pani-NR composite exhibited an overpotential at a current density of 10 mA cm−2 (η10) of 196 mV for HER and 160 mV for OER. The Tafel slopes were 146 and 118 mV dec−1 for HER and OER, respectively, demonstrating excellent electrocatalytic activity and stability over a 48 hours testing period. The total water splitting using a two electrode system connected to a DC-power supply showed an Ecell equal to 2.12 V@10 mA. In the capacitive energy storage domain, the composite exhibited a specific capacitance of 373 F g−1 at 0.5 A g−1, with a potential window of 0.6 V. The material demonstrated a rate capability of 77.3% (0.5–5 A g−1) and a capacitance retention of 86% after 10 000 cycles at 10 A g−1. These results confirm the material's remarkable stability and potential for long-term application in energy storage and conversion technologies.
